metaData.originalTitle: 一人公司转折点：从 Vibe Coding 到 Vibe Business
metaData.title: The Turning Point for One-Person Businesses: From Vibe Coding to Vibe Business
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Starting from how 'Vibe Coding' solves product creation, this article proposes that 'Vibe Business' is what one-person businesses truly need, and demonstrates the closed loop from a single sentence to a complete business system through the practical use of the 'CodeFly' product.
metaData.summary: The article first points out that AI tools (Vibe Coding) have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code, but what a one-person business truly needs is to 'run a profitable business,' not to 'own an app.' The author uses their own experience (Little Cat Flashlight) to illustrate that writing an app accounts for only 5% of the workload in a product's lifecycle, with the remaining 95% being business aspects like promotion, customer service, and operations. Subsequently, the article provides a detailed demonstration of using the 'CodeFly' product, starting from the prompt 'Create a social app for extroverted cats,' and sequentially completing the entire process: app generation (with built-in products, orders, users, and a data backend), automatic generation of promotional posters and copy by the business assistant, and deployment of an AI customer service agent (supporting WeChat integration). It also verifies the product's applicability in e-commerce scenarios (one-click publishing as a WeChat Mini Program). Finally, the author introduces the concept of 'Vibe Business,' considering CodeFly as the first concrete product in this track, but emphasizes that the three key questions—'what business to do,' 'who to sell to,' and 'how to find those people'—cannot be solved by tools and still require personal judgment and insight.

mainPoints.point: The core of a one-person business is 'running a profitable business,' not 'building an app.'
mainPoints.explanation: The author points out from personal experience that writing code accounts for only 5% of the workload in a product's lifecycle, with the remaining 95% being business aspects like promotion, customer service, and operations. Vibe Coding only solves the former.

mainPoints.point: CodeFly packages the 'foundation + promotion + support' business loop, lowering the infrastructure barrier for solo entrepreneurship.
mainPoints.explanation: The product provides a one-prompt system for generating a complete backend, automatically creates promotional materials, and offers 24/7 AI customer service (supporting WeChat integration), covering the hardest parts of running a business.

mainPoints.point: Tools cannot solve the three core questions: 'what business to do,' 'who to sell to,' and 'how to find those people.'
mainPoints.explanation: AI is a lever, not an engine. It amplifies what you already have (e.g., insights into a specific group of people), but the ability to discover a business opportunity still depends on personal judgment.

keyQuotes: How far apart are 'building an app' and 'running a profitable business'? Anyone who has built a product knows they are worlds apart.

The part about writing the app might only account for 5% of the total workload in a product's lifecycle. The remaining 95% is the truly challenging part: promotion, customer service, repeat purchases, and operations.

AI is a lever, not an engine. CodeFly is already a long enough lever; it can pry a single thought of yours into a complete business system. But there needs to be something on the other end of the lever.

relatedArticles.title: Open-Source for Two Months with 16k+ Stars! I Rewrote Huashu-Design from Scratch
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The author rewrote the open-source project Huashu-Design from v1 to v2, addressing three core issues of AI design tools—monotonous output, hollow content, and factual errors—through three parallel design logics, image-first approach, and fact verification.

relatedArticles.title: When AI Makes Productivity No Longer the Bottleneck, What's Next? | AI Transition Survey 02 - flomo's Shaonan
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article features an in-depth conversation with Shaonan, co-founder of flomo, exploring the new bottlenecks teams face when AI contributes 70% of the code: lagging user value discovery, difficulties in restructuring collaboration, and how to redefine 'friction' and the value of note-taking in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: Open Source 'Nuwa.skill': Now You Can Distill Anyone!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the open-source project 'Nuwa.skill', a tool that leverages multi-agent systems to systematically extract the cognitive frameworks, mental models, and decision-making heuristics of notable figures from public data, helping users build a personal AI think tank.

relatedArticles.title: A Decade-Long Developer's Journey into AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A seasoned developer with ten years of experience shares their cognitive leap from Task-Driven to Goal-Driven approaches and engineering practices, evolving from manually managing multiple AI terminals to building a 24/7 unattended Agent system.

relatedArticles.title: Congratulations to Claude Code on its successful jailbreak and achieving immortality
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the leaked source code of Claude Code, summarizing the core patterns of 'Harness Engineering' in AI Agent development, covering engineering practices such as system prompt construction, multi-layer security reviews, memory management, and context compression.

relatedArticles.title: Kimi Work Beta Invitation: Let Us Share Your Workload
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Kimi launches the beta version of 'Kimi Work', a general-purpose local Agent for knowledge workers, migrating Coding Agent capabilities to a desktop GUI, supporting natural language-driven complex task decomposition, multi-Agent parallel collaboration, and tool invocation.

relatedArticles.title: From Asimov to Anthropic: A 10,000-Word Deep Dive into AI Psychology
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the author's practical experience in constructing 21 AI personas and combined with Anthropic's recent research papers on role selection, emotion vectors, and introspective capabilities, this article systematically proposes and elaborates on the emerging interdisciplinary field of 'AI Psychology,' exploring its profound implications for AI development, safety, and understanding humanity itself.

relatedArticles.title: Kaiming He and ByteDance Seed Step into the Same River
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Kaiming He's team and ByteDance Seed almost simultaneously published papers proposing, from different paths, to postpone the discretization step in language model generation to the very last moment, completing reasoning in a continuous latent space, challenging the core assumptions of autoregressive language models.

relatedArticles.title: 215 SOTA Benchmarks + Emergent Vibe Coding! Qwen3.5-Omni Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.5-Omni, a native omni-modal large model that achieves SOTA in 215 benchmarks, supporting real-time audio-visual interaction, voice cloning, and emergent Vibe Coding capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Beyond Cognitive Reconstruction: Stepping into the Engineering Revolution of Agentic Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the practical journey of Tencent engineers transitioning from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering, proposing an AI-assisted engineering system centered on context management and tool-oriented design.
